entities.summary: Stanley George Payne is an American historian of modern Spain and European fascism at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. He retired from full-time teaching in 2004 and is currently Professor Emeritus at its Department of History. His works on the Spanish Civil War and the Francoist period received various estimates: while by the 1980s he had earned the reputation of "America's most prolific historian of Spain", in the 21st century his later works became known for their "revisionist" approach and received criticism from some historians as overly benevolent towards Francoism and spreading Francoist narratives.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Stanley George Payne's works on the Spanish Civil War and Francoist period have had a significant regional impact, influencing the understanding of modern Spain and European fascism. His revisionist approach has sparked debate among historians, contributing to ongoing discussions about the legacy of Francoism.
